mbm-0801.clue: I let the ducks play through.
mbm-0801.quote: Three ducklings marched between my ball and the golf cup. I stood with my putter tucked under my arm until the last one crossed. Best excuse I’ve ever had for a slow round.

mbm-0802.clue: I count bridges with shoelace knots.
mbm-0802.quote: I tied a loose loop in my spare lace at every footbridge on my long run. By the seventh I had a little chain. I hung it above the door to remember how far my feet took me.

mbm-0803.clue: I play better with a crooked line.
mbm-0803.quote: A little boy marked our beach volleyball court with a shell and drew one side in waves. We argued about every close ball and invited him back to referee the rematch.

mbm-0804.clue: My job started with an apple on my head.
mbm-0804.quote: I sat for an art class in a red sweater. The teacher added an apple for balance. Twenty minutes later every drawing had a solemn model trying desperately to keep a straight face.

mbm-0805.clue: I give my books a second set of ears.
mbm-0805.quote: I read pirate stories aloud to my granddad while he mends fishing nets. When I skip a sentence, he stops tying knots. He knows exactly where the treasure is.

mbm-0806.clue: I found my mother’s old wooden driver.
mbm-0806.quote: The grip still has a strip of blue tape where her thumb sat. We took it out together at dawn and she beat my drive by a good ten yards in her gardening shoes.

mbm-0807.clue: I keep a spare crown in my card box.
mbm-0807.quote: My little sister drew a paper crown for the field mouse on my weakest fantasy card. I played it first, just so she could see the mouse get its royal entrance.

mbm-0808.clue: I can tell you what the windsock had for lunch.
mbm-0808.quote: A grocery bag snagged on the pole at our airfield and made a second tiny windsock. I sketched both in my flight log. The little one was the better weather vane that morning.

mbm-0809.clue: I found a second sun in my beach bag.
mbm-0809.quote: My uncle gave me a pocket mirror for signaling from across the beach. We use it to flash hello from our lounge chairs. His hello always arrives halfway through my nap.

mbm-0810.clue: I’ve never traded the card with a coffee ring.
mbm-0810.quote: Dad drew a sea monster inside a coffee stain on my card sleeve. I slide it over a different creature each game. The monster has swallowed just about everyone in my deck.

mbm-0811.clue: I keep the shell pick for quiet afternoons.
mbm-0811.quote: I tried my first cuatro tune on the porch with a shell-shaped pick. My aunt called the tune from the street below. By the last chorus we had three voices and only four chairs.

mbm-0812.clue: I pack the picnic in a round tin.
mbm-0812.quote: My sister and I paddled our canoe into a bed of lilies and ate biscuits from a round blue tin. A frog hopped aboard. We let him ride all the way back to the landing.

mbm-0813.clue: I know which stone makes a good bell.
mbm-0813.quote: From my kayak I heard waves tapping a hollow rock under the cliff. I drifted there with my paddle across my knees until I could hum the whole rhythm.

mbm-0814.clue: I hang my watch on the cold side.
mbm-0814.quote: After a snowy hike I left my watch in the onsen changing room and watched the steam melt snow on the rocks instead. That little patch of stone gave me the whole afternoon.

mbm-0815.clue: I once played eighteen holes with one tee.
mbm-0815.quote: Dad carved my golf tee from a snapped blue pencil. I carried it through a whole round without losing it. The last little bit of lead drew a star on my scorecard.

mbm-0816.clue: I look for the cracks first.
mbm-0816.quote: In a museum of ceramics I found a vase repaired with bright golden seams. I went home and drew our chipped sugar bowl as though it belonged under the very same light.

mbm-0817.clue: I wore out a pair of yellow socks on a song.
mbm-0817.quote: My sister smiled whenever the yellow yarn on my marimba mallets bounced past her. At Christmas she knitted me matching socks. We wore them thin dancing after the concert.

mbm-0818.quote: I entered the pancake contest with Dad. At the last pancake we both slowed down because Grandma had cooked it, and it was too good to hurry. We split the little bronze fork.

mbm-0819.clue: My aunt gave the bunker a name.
mbm-0819.quote: I spent three shots in one sand trap. She stuck a tiny paper umbrella in it and called it my holiday home. I keep the umbrella in my golf bag for our return visit.

mbm-0820.clue: I know which plate is the noisy one.
mbm-0820.quote: One iron weight in our gym rings like a bell when I set it down. After my first clean set my training partner tapped it with a knuckle. Everybody turned and clapped.

mbm-0821.quote: I crocheted a gray cloud tea cozy with three little blue raindrops. When the kettle steams, the drops swing. The kids stop talking halfway through the story to watch the weather.

mbm-0822.clue: I listen for the train with the cracked bell.
mbm-0822.quote: The little local has a bell that sings two different notes. Grandpa and I take cocoa to the footbridge on Saturdays. I can usually name the engine before he sees it.

mbm-0823.clue: I can find the smallest exhibit in the room.
mbm-0823.quote: At the science museum I leaned into a magnifying lens and found a little clock inside a gold ring. I waited until my friend got a turn before I told her it actually ticked.

mbm-0824.clue: I’ve bowled in mittens in July.
mbm-0824.quote: Our alley held a costume night. I turned up as a snowman and tucked my yarn mittens into my belt before rolling. When the last pin fell I put them back on for high fives.

mbm-0825.clue: I got a second controller for my birthday.
mbm-0825.quote: Grandma liked my puzzle game but couldn’t manage the fast buttons. I move the pieces while she calls the gaps. Together we built a tower clear to the little pixel moon.
